items.title: List commands and spans in the run statistics package

goal.title: List commands and spans in the run statistics package
criteria: Listing commands over a logs directory with two runs and a day of standalone commands gives every command, oldest first. Each carries its run, workflow, step, step moved to, arguments, timing, exit code and any error message, and a standalone command has no run.

Listing spans gives every helper, user-wait and work span in runs and outside them, each with its run, step, task, parent and outcome. An unfinished span is capped and marked exactly as the run report marks it.
A run selection narrows both listings to that run's records, and asking only for records outside runs gives just the orchestrator's.
The run report, comparison and summary output is unchanged for the same logs.
The structured form of both listings uses exactly the field names in the plan's Data Structures section.

scope.rule: Change only the files that belong to this item; change nothing that belongs to another task.

verdicts.evidence: listings.go:87-112 Commands gathers every run's Commands plus l.Outside command records (listed() includes outside records when no selection is given), then sorts by StartedAt. commandRow (listings.go:115-142) fills run_id/kind/name only when run != nil, so standalone commands get nulls. It carries step (AttrStep), step_to (AttrStepTo), args (stringsAttr over AttrCommandArgs), duration, exit code (intAttr, with 1 for an error status lacking an exit code) and message (kept only for StatusError). listings_test.go:93-133 asserts the seven-command oldest-first order over the two-run plus standalone fixture (listingLogs, lines 38-83) and checks the standalone fields, the goto's step/step_to, and the refused command's exit 1 and message.

listings.go:147-175 AgentSpans covers run spans and l.Outside spans, filtered by tracelog.AgentTypes (record.go:45: sub-agent, user-wait, work). Each row is built by waitRow, which supplies step, task, parent, end reason, status and complete, plus type, trace, run, kind and workflow. Outside spans are capped in outsideSpans (listings.go:180-221): an unfinished span ends at the last event of its own trace and never before its start. Run spans reuse capUnfinished from assemble.go:313-328, and the rendered end marker is the same unfinishedMark used by the run report (render.go:21, 183). listings_test.go:180-237 checks the open helper in the run (ih) matches the run report's helper row exactly, and the outside open span (oh2) is capped at its start.

listings.go:73-84 listed(): a run selection (f.selected()) narrows to l.Candidates(f) with outside=false; outsideRuns with no selection returns only outside records (runs nil, outside true). listings_test.go:146-167 checks Filter{Name:"000002_beta"} gives 3 rows all with the implement run id, Filter{Runs:[prefix]} gives 2 rows, and Commands(Filter{}, true) gives exactly the two epic commands with nil run_id. listings_test.go:239-259 checks the same for AgentSpans. listings.go:75-76 refuses outsideRuns combined with a selection (CodeBadSelection, select.go:47-48).

The report, comparison and summary paths only move code without changing it. assemble.go splitTrace (lines 69-106) is the old buildRun loop moved into a helper, and report.go waitRow (lines 229-243) is the old wait-building block moved verbatim. Load keeps the runs identical: assemble.go:96-108 only collects the outside records. listings_test.go:263-282 (TestOutsideRecordsLeaveRunsUnchanged) checks that runs, BuildReport, Compare and Summarise are equal with and without the outside records. The existing golden tests (report.golden.json, compare.golden.json, summary.golden.json, and the txt goldens) are not in the diff, so they are unchanged and still pass. Scope observation: report.go and select.go are modified but are not in the goal's file list. The changes are the waitRow extraction and the CodeBadSelection message, which the listings need, so this is not a criterion failure.

The JSON field names come from struct tags. CommandRow (listings.go:32-49) has run_id, kind, name, agent, span_id, parent_span_id, command, args, step, step_to, started_at, ended_at, duration_ms, exit_code, status, message. SpanRow (listings.go:55-62) embeds Wait and adds type, trace_id, run_id, kind, workflow. listings_test.go:287-307 pins those key sets, and both golden files (testdata/commands.golden.json, testdata/spans.golden.json) use exactly those keys. The code comment at listings.go:16-29 quotes the contract as the plan's Data Structures section. I did not open the plan itself because the repo's rules forbid reading store files with my own tools, so this verdict rests on the code's quoted contract and the pinning tests.

items.title: List commands and spans from the command line

goal.title: List commands and spans from the command line
criteria: `stats commands` and `stats spans` show the fixture project's records in table and JSON form, with the same figures in both, and the JSON honours `--fields`.
Pointing `--dir` at a copy of the logs from outside any project gives the same output as in the project.
Combining a run selection with the outside-runs switch is refused with a message naming the fix, and the other refusals match the rest of the group.
Every log file is byte-identical before and after both commands, run inside a project with logging on.

scope.rule: Change only the files that belong to this item; change nothing that belongs to another task.

verdicts.evidence: cmd/stats.go:272-316 (runStatsCommands and runStatsSpans) renders the same logs.Commands/logs.AgentSpans rows as a table (runstats.RenderCommands/RenderSpans, internal/runstats/render.go:572-619) or as JSON via output.New(...).WriteResult with globalFields, so --fields applies. cmd/stats_test.go:263-299 checks the pretty table columns and the JSON duration_ms (60000) and exit_code for the same record, and TestStatsCommandsListsEveryCommandInBothForms checks --fields ["commands"] yields only that key. cmd/stats_test.go:301-339 does the same for spans (25m00s / 25*60000 for the stopped orchestrator span, 3m00s / 180000 for the helper) and checks --fields ["spans"]. Table and JSON are asserted against the same fixture values, though no single test compares the two outputs directly.

cmd/stats_test.go:400-416 (TestStatsListingsDirOnACopyGiveTheSameOutput) takes the in-project JSON for commands and spans, copies the logs with copyLogs (line 308) to a directory, does t.Chdir(t.TempDir()) outside any project, runs with --dir, and requires the output equal to the in-project output except log_dir. cmd/stats.go:476-514 (statsLogs) only needs a project when --dir is absent.

A run selection with --outside-runs is refused in internal/runstats/listings.go:75-76 (CodeBadSelection). internal/runstats/select.go:47-48 gives the message "--outside-runs lists only the records written outside any workflow run, so it cannot be combined with a run selection" (names the flag). cmd/stats.go:539-542 maps it to stats_bad_selection with the next action "use --outside-runs on its own, or drop it and select runs with --name, --kind, --agent or --run", the same code and envelope as the other selection refusals (bad kind, bad run id, run not found, ambiguous) at cmd/stats.go:523-538. cmd/stats_test.go:370-398 checks the code, next action and message for both commands, and the other refusals (format, missing dir, bad kind, unknown and ambiguous run) for both subcommands.

cmd/stats.go:76-98 and 273-316: statsCommandsCmd and statsSpansCmd are added to statsCmd, so they inherit the logging-exempt annotation (cmd/stats.go:21-23, 25-27). cmd/stats_test.go:418-430 (TestStatsListingsLeaveTheLogsByteIdentical) runs useConfiguredLogLevel with a verbose project, snapshots every log with rawLogSnapshot, runs commands and spans in pretty, JSON, --outside-runs and --kind forms, and requires the snapshot unchanged. No code path in the diff writes to the logs directory.

goal.title: Harbor run log reader
criteria: Given `stats` output for an epic trial, the reader shows each lane's start, finish, children and the step each earlier child stopped at, with a resume counted from a failed workflow start in that lane.

Each child is matched to the orchestrator helper span open when it began, including a resumed lane's later child, children launched together and a span never stopped, and the orchestrator's next command or span after a finished lane is found.
Merges, the steps a plan entered and changelog writes per repo match what the old session-log rules gave for the same run.
A missing binary, a missing logs directory, a `stats` refusal, a timeout or unreadable output each produce a stated reason rather than an empty result.
The reader reads the logs only through `stats`, and an integration test with a freshly built binary over fixture logs gives the same answers as the canned responses.

scope.rule: Change only the files that belong to this item; change nothing that belongs to another task.

verdicts.evidence: tests/harbor/shared/runlog.py:166-175 (Lane fields start, finish, children, stops) and :377-385 (_settle): start is the first successful `<kind> new`, finish the first successful move to `finished`, stops has one entry per later child (failed new gives its step or "?", a restart gives "restart"). tests/harbor/shared/tests/test_runlog.py:200-212 asserts alpha and beta start, finish, children 2, stops ["architecture"] and the resume at at(11) against the fixture trial. A failed `new` after the start is counted as a resume (runlog.py:383), so the resume-from-failed-start rule holds.

runlog.py:277-297 (_child_spans) matches children in first-command order to the earliest unmatched orchestrator span open at the child's start, with open_at (runlog.py:149-152) treating a never-stopped span as open from its start. runlog.py:307-326 (orchestrator_reaction) takes the first outside-run epic/trace command, other-spec command or orchestrator span edge after lane.last.end. test_runlog.py:246-263 covers launched-together (ob1 for beta, oa kept by alpha), the resumed later child (ob2, not complete), and no open span. test_runlog.py:274-296 covers the reaction rules.

test_runlog.py:403-439 (test_the_reader_agrees_with_the_old_session_log_rules) runs the old tests/harbor/shared/sessionlog.py rules over a verbose copy of the same fixture trial and asserts equality of start, finish, children, stops, resume times, merge per spec, plan_steps_entered vs steps_entered("plan"), and changelog_writes_by_repo for ALPHA, BETA and None. The reader mirrors the old rules: runlog.py:332-339 vs sessionlog.py:283-290 and runlog.py:341-363 vs sessionlog.py:294-316. The verification run reports test_runlog.py 44 passed. Minor divergence, not a failure: runlog.py:385 always reports a successful later `new` as "restart", while sessionlog.py:226 uses that segment's first state_before step when present; the parity fixture does not exercise this.

runlog.py:215 (no binary: reason naming SPEKTACULAR_BIN), :217 (no logs directory: "no Spektacular logs at <dir>"), :234 (refusal: "stats <sub>: <code>: <message>"), :223-224 (timeout: "took longer than 60s"), :225-230 (OSError and non-JSON output each raise Unavailable with a reason). test_runlog.py:137-182 asserts each of these reasons, including the parametrised unreadable-output cases.

runlog.py:218-221 is the only route to the logs: it runs `<binary> stats <sub> ... --dir <logs> --format json`, and the module never opens files (test_runlog.py:397-400 asserts the source has no open(, read_text, glob, iterdir). tests/harbor/shared/tests/test_runlog_integration.py:36-40 builds a fresh binary with go build from the repo root, and :75-80 asserts views() from the real binary equal the canned answers from runlog_fixtures.stats(). Lines 84-87 check a copied logs directory gives the same answers. The verification run reports test_runlog_integration.py 3 passed, not skipped. The Go JSON field names used by runlog.py match the json tags in internal/runstats/listings.go:33-61.

goal.title: Metrics record from Spektacular's logs
criteria: For a trial whose logs hold a spec run with a helper and a user wait, the record's steps and step timings equal the run statistics report for those logs, and each step shows working, helper-wait and user-wait time adding up to its duration.
Every helper is listed with its spec and step, including one an epic orchestrator started outside any run, and each step shows how many helpers it started.
The record reports total user-wait, helper-wait and gap time in place of the single longest gap.
With the logs removed, every step, helper and wait measure is unknown with a reason, none is filled in from the transcript, the recorder exits successfully, and the reward is untouched.
Token usage, models and cost equal the pinned figures for every reference run.
The same logs paired with a Claude, a Bob and a Codex transcript give identical steps and helper sections.

scope.rule: Change only the files that belong to this item; change nothing that belongs to another task.

verdicts.evidence: tests/harbor/shared/metrics.py step_rows() (around line 425) takes duration_ms, helper_wait_ms and user_wait_ms from the `stats run` report and writes working_s = duration - helper - user. Those JSON keys match internal/runstats/report.go tags. test_metrics.py test_steps_equal_the_run_report_and_each_split_adds_up checks each step against fx.spec_report() and asserts the split sums to duration_s on the spec trial, which has both a 120 s user wait and a 180 s helper wait. Caveat: working_s is floored at 0 (metrics.py max(0, ...)), so the sum only equals the duration when waits do not overlap; test_working_time_is_floored_at_zero_when_waits_overlap shows the overlap case. The criterion's trial has no overlap, so it holds for that trial.

metrics.py helper_record() (around line 491) writes span_id, parent, name, spec, kind, step, task_id, outside_run, times and status for every sub-agent span. For a span with run_id None it takes spec from the child launched under it or the lane whose first run started during it, and sets step to null. read_logs() (around line 570) builds the helper list from log.spans(). step_rows() counts helpers per step from each run report's helpers list. test_metrics.py test_an_orchestrators_helpers_take_the_lane_of_their_child covers the epic trial's outside-run helpers, and test_each_step_counts_the_helpers_started_in_it covers the per-step counts.

metrics.py read_logs() (around line 548) writes totals user_wait_s, helper_wait_s, gap_s, gaps and gap_threshold_s, summed over every workflow run. The idle_s field and its idle_seconds computation are removed from build_record. test_metrics.py test_totals_sum_the_waits_and_gaps_of_every_run asserts these totals and asserts 'idle_s' not in totals. README.md (Run metrics totals row, around line 16) documents the three measures.

metrics.py no_logs() (around line 483) nulls the workflows, totals, subagents and trace sections and lists each LOG_FIELDS entry as Unknown with the reason. read_logs_safely() catches recorder errors the same way. read_logs() returns no_logs when runlog raises Unavailable, and never reads transcript data into those fields. main() always returns 0 and never writes the reward. test_metrics.py test_logs_that_cannot_answer_leave_every_log_measure_unknown and test_logs_removed_leave_the_log_measures_unknown_for_every_agent cover removed logs, and the reward is asserted unchanged; the transcript's totals and briefs are asserted to survive.

test_reference_runs.py test_reference_totals_are_pinned and test_reference_record_totals_match_the_pins_without_spektacular_logs compare each record's model, token totals and cost to PINNED_TOTALS for every reference run. The PINNED_TOTALS block is unchanged in the diff. The verification summary reports 613 passed for tests/harbor/shared/tests. I did not re-run the tests; this verdict rests on the test code and the passing run.

test_metrics.py test_the_same_logs_give_the_same_steps_and_helpers_for_every_agent runs claude, bob, codex, codex-rollout and oracle through agent_trial() with the same stats answers (spec and epic). It asserts steps, helpers and log_sections equal the Claude record for every agent, and that records differ only in transcript totals and briefs. The verification summary reports this suite passing. I did not re-run it.

goal.title: Delegation checks judge from spans

An epic lane with no orchestrator helper running when it started fails, naming the spec.
A spec review child whose brief lacks the staged spec, and an implementing child whose brief lacks its worktree folder, are still reported.
Self-checks fail if the worktree-folder constant or the required-step list drifts from the code and templates they mirror.

items.title: Suite verifiers read the logs through stats

goal.title: Suite verifiers read the logs through stats
criteria: No suite verifier or verifier self-check imports the old session-log reader or reads `.spektacular/debug`.
Every check that read a response or a state snapshot now reads a fact recorded at the default log level, and its pass and fail outcomes are unchanged on the self-check fixtures.
The epic suite no longer checks for `status <epic>` polls, and no verifier reads a `status` command from the logs.
Each suite's self-check passes against fake readers built from canned `stats` output.

scope.rule: Change only the files that belong to this item; change nothing that belongs to another task.

verdicts.evidence: The suite verifiers themselves are clean: no tests/harbor/*/tests/test_*.py outside shared imports sessionlog or spans (grep), and test_runlog.py:538-543 guards that. But verifier self-checks still import the old reader. tests/harbor/shared/tests/test_sessionlog_rules.py:44 is `from sessionlog import SessionLog, changelog_writes_by_repo, plan_steps_entered, read_events`. That file pins the verifier rules 'through the verifier's own test function' and reads debug fixtures at lines 150 (`S55_PLAN / "debug"`) and 235 (`S55_IMPLEMENT / "debug"`). tests/harbor/shared/tests/test_runlog.py:426 also does `import sessionlog` inside the module that holds the verifier self-checks (from line 442). The diff leaves all of this in place.

The reads moved to default-level facts. test_goal_check.py:204 uses e.args instead of the logged command text. test_implement_epic_workflow.py:525 uses e.step != "update_plan" in place of state_before. test_plan_workflow.py:1390 uses RunLog.steps_entered (step_to of successful plan commands). test_spec_workflow.py:6541-6546 uses runs, report steps and user-wait spans. test_standing_rules.py:6584 uses c.args. The response-based worktree and walkthrough checks are gone. The reader's canned-answer self-checks in test_runlog.py:484-535 keep the old pass and fail cases (skips-walkthrough, finished-first, never-finished, no lane, changelog removed or failed).
